claims.claim: Chow says if re-elected she would make the city's student nutrition program universal by 2030 and extend it to cover lunches
Chow did not say what the expansion would cost taxpayers
The program serves about 330,000 students daily with the city contributing $32 million this year
In 2024-2025 the city received $4.7M federal and $8.5M provincial for school food, and was the largest funder at $21.9M, raised to $32M in the 2026 budget
claims.attributed_to: CBC News / Toronto Public Health presentation

claims.claim: Council authorized receiving a USD $1.2M (CAD $1,643,720) Bloomberg Philanthropies award for the universal school food program
Ontario funds its Student Nutrition Programs at $37.5 million in 2025-26, serving more than 800,000 students provincewide
Neither the federal government nor the province would say whether they are committed to funding an expansion
Bradford says he supports the idea but the mayor has not said how the city would pay for it
Bradford has pledged to freeze property tax rates in his first year and scrap the land transfer tax for homes under $1.1 million
Council approved a 2024 motion directing staff toward a universal lunch program by 2030
claims.attributed_to: Urban Mag, citing Toronto Star reporting
